newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel slows E Jerusalem plan, agrees to PLO talks.
newsitem.headline: Israel slows E Jerusalem plan, agrees to PLO talks.

text.p: Israel on Monday put the brakes on a plan to build a new Jewish enclave in Arab East Jerusalem and agreed to resume talks with the PLO on meeting commitments made under their interim peace deals.

While the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) praised the moves as steps to restore confidence, it stressed that the sides were far from surmounting a months-long deadlock on proceeding with final peace talks.

Israel's Interior Ministry suspended a permit granted to a U.S. Jewish land baron to build 70 Jewish homes in Ras al-Amoud, a 11,000-strong Arab neighbourhood on the slopes of the Mount of Olives, until an appeal against the plan had been heard.
Palestinians, who want East Jerusalem as capital of a future state, have said the project would bury Middle East peace moves.
Suspension of the plan, though technical, bought time for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to try to defuse the latest crisis in Israel's embittered relations with the Palestinians.

"We feel that stopping the action there contributes to the confidence that is being built," senior PLO negotiator Nabil Shaath told reporters after talks with Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy in a Jerusalem hotel.
Levy and Shaath agreed that joint Israeli-PLO committees would renew talks on outstanding issues from a 1995 peace deal.
They include the opening of Gaza air and sea ports, a "safe passage" for Palestinians between the West Bank and Gaza Strip and the release of Palestinian prisoners held by Israel.
Levy said Israel agreed to the move after receiving assurances from Palestinian President Yasser Arafat that he would cooperate with Israel in "the war on terror".
He said Arafat had made arrests and opened a probe into a PLO police cell Israel alleged had launched attacks on Jews.

Shaath said the resumption of committees signalled "the desire to go the second phase" but said: "The issues upon which this deadlock developed still await solution: the issues of settlement, Jerusalem, and the return to (final) negotiations".

Israeli-PLO peace talks have been in crisis since March when Israel broke ground on a 6,500-home settlement on an East Jerusalem hill known to Israelis as Har Homa and to Palestinians as Jabal Abu Ghneim.

Palestinians demand a halt to settlement activity as the price to restart peace talks. Israel, which annexed East Jerusalem after capturing it in 1967, says it can build where it likes in the city it calls its united capital.

Netanyahu, who vowed to block the Ras al-Amoud plan after being surprised by the Jerusalem municipality's decision to grant a permit to U.S. magnate Irving Moskowitz, was forced to fend off right-wing criticism he had gone soft on Jerusalem.

"What is first and foremost important to understand that we want to build in Jerusalem and we will continue to build in Jerusalem...(Ras al-Amoud) is not the right place and it's not the right time," Netanyahu told Israel Television.
Netanyahu has said work will continue at Har Homa.
Saeb Erekat, the PLO's senior negotiator, accused Netanyahu of using the Ras al-Amoud project to appear "dovish" to the world and divert attention from the larger settlement.
"If settlement activities continue, there really would be no peace process. Any peace intiative has to include a halt to settlement activities," Erekat told Reuters.

The Jerusalem District Appeal Committee is due to hold a preliminary hearing on the challenge to the Ras al-Amoud project, filed on Sunday by two left-wing members of the Jerusalem city council, on August 5.
Moskowitz, a Miami-based businessman who finances Jewish settlement in occupied territories, said on Monday that efforts to block his project played into Palestinian hands.

"If this is not a good time for building a Jewish neighbourhood on Har Hazeitim (Mount of Olives), the Arabs will feel they won a victory by their threats and intimidations and they will do everything possible to stop the project at Har Homa," he told Israel Radio before the suspension.
